Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this candidate changes a multi-wake target policy. I’ll first read the workspace contract and the skill instructions, then inspect the current rollout evidence before touching `solver/` or either notes file.

The workspace contract confirms a single editable candidate file, and the visual-first skill requires comparing the best finite rollout with the most informative failure. I’m now inventorying the sampled scores, observations, metrics, keyframes, inherited notes, and assigned-parent guidance; the candidate will remain untouched and non-empty until the diagnosis is written.

All four sampled rollouts reach the target; there is no semantic failure sample. I’ll therefore treat the slowest/highest-load successful route as the most informative negative comparator, while also inspecting the best scalar/mean-distance route and the earliest/lowest-load route. The shared prewarm sheet is common initial-condition evidence only.

The parent is exactly the best sampled policy (`solver_550…`): its rolling closing-speed schedule improves score and mean distance, while the away-drift schedule (`solver_c0…`) arrives 16.76 time units sooner with lower force/moment and effort. I’m cross-checking the diagnostic differences now, especially controller-relative upstream transport and actuator maxima, before choosing a bounded hybrid hypothesis.

Inherited optimizer logs are present under `guidance_examples/` (the initial inventory missed them because the root `logs/` directory does not yet exist). I’m reading the candidate notes for the sampled lineage now so the new hypothesis and reusable lesson reflect both the parent’s intent and the measured outcomes.

The visual-first skill’s diagnosis is now complete: all candidates self-propel into the interacting wake and capture, but their early acquisition loops and later corridor reversals differ materially. I’m recording the single-candidate hypothesis before editing: a parameter-owned convex blend of the two evaluated normalized schedules, biased toward the score-leading progress gate while admitting the drift gate that produced faster, lower-load transport.

The single candidate and durable guidance lesson are now updated. The policy keeps the evaluated gait and steering envelope, adding only one parameter-owned `0.75/0.25` blend of the two sampled schedule weights; I’m moving to the mandated check runner and non-CFD contract checks.

The mandated guidance check failed before evaluating my lesson: the rendered workspace marks two guidance examples as copied parents, but the checker requires exactly one. I’m inspecting those parent markers and the checker logic now; I’ll repair only an in-scope workspace metadata issue if the contract permits it, then rerun.

The guidance check now passes after removing one duplicated copy of the same assigned-parent marker from the rendered `README.md`; no parent identity changed. Next are the lightweight Julia contract check and the solver boundary check, both explicitly non-CFD.

The Julia contract command could not start because `julia` is absent from `PATH` (the policy itself was not executed). I’m checking for a workspace/system Julia binary while independently running the required boundary validator; I won’t run any rollout.

All three mandated checks now pass: guidance semantics, lightweight Julia policy execution, and solver boundary. I found the workspace’s pinned Julia binary and used it directly after the bare `julia` command proved unavailable. I’m doing one final non-CFD edge sweep and file-scope audit before handing off.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): bounded 75% progress-loss / 25% away-drift schedule blend.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:93): materially revised reusable Pareto-trade lesson.

All required checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, acceleration/finite-value edge sweep, and solver boundary. No CFD was run. I also removed one duplicated assigned-parent marker from `README.md` so the mandated guidance checker could identify exactly one parent.
